title: Erdős #1 OQ-01: Sum Bound and Monotonicity for Distinct Subset Sums
description: Extends Erdős #1 with tighter results: sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 for n-element DSS sets (sum bound), monotonicity (subsets of DSS sets are DSS), and the counting bound as a corollary. Small case verifications. 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős's $500 problem: for n elements with all 2^n subset sums distinct, must max(A) ≥ c·2^n? Dubroff-Fox-Xu (2021) proved the lower bound N ≥ √(2/π)·2^n/√n. The Conway-Guy sequence gives N ≤ 0.22009·2^n.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 for n-element DSS sets (stronger than element-wise bound). (2) Subsets of DSS sets are DSS (monotonicity).
overview.proofStrategy: Sum bound: the 2^n distinct sums are non-negative integers in [0, sum(A)], so sum(A)+1 ≥ 2^n. Monotonicity: if distinct subsets of A have different sums, so do distinct subsets of B ⊆ A. Counting: max(A) ≥ sum(A)/n ≥ (2^n−1)/n.
keyInsights: **Tighter sum bound**: sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 is stronger than n·max(A) ≥ 2^n since max(A) ≤ sum(A)/n (harmonic mean bound).
**Monotonicity**: DSS is preserved under taking subsets — key for inductive arguments about DSS set structure.
**Injection argument**: all 2^n subsets have distinct sums in [0, sum(A)] → sum(A) ≥ 2^n − 1 by pigeonhole.

sections.summary: distinct_subset_sums_sum_bound: 2^n ≤ sum(A)+1. dss_monotone: B ⊆ A → DSS(A) → DSS(B). counting_bound_corollary.
sections.mathContext: $|A| = n$, DSS $\Rightarrow$ $\text{sum}(A) \geq 2^n - 1$; DSS sets are closed under subsets.

conclusion.summary: 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Sum bound 2^n ≤ sum(A)+1 and DSS monotonicity proved.
conclusion.implications: The sum bound and monotonicity are structural results that constrain the shape of extremal DSS sets.
openQuestions: Can the Dubroff-Fox-Xu bound N ≥ 2^n·√(2/π)/√n be formally proved?
Can the Conway-Guy conjecture be verified computationally for all n ≤ 100?
Can the DSS condition be connected to B_h set theory?
